tools.name: ship_check
tools.description: Before shipping, or right after deploying, an app built with Lovable, Bolt, Cursor, v0, Replit, Claude Code or similar, run ship_check on the live URL. It scans the deployed app from the outside, the way a visitor or attacker sees it, and returns a launch-readiness report where every finding has a status and a concrete fix. It reads the homepage plus up to 19 more of the app's own pages (links and sitemap, robots.txt respected) and every same-origin script those pages load. Checks: (1) secret keys exposed in that code, with the file they were found in (Stripe live secret, restricted and webhook keys, Stripe test secret keys, AWS, OpenAI, Anthropic, GitHub, SendGrid and Slack keys, Supabase secret and service_role keys, hardcoded bearer tokens and passwords); (2) open database access: if the code ships a Supabase URL and public anon or publishable key, whether the common tables profiles and users return rows to that key without login (a missing Row Level Security policy; count only, no row data is read; a service_role key is never used); (3) pages and APIs open without login: one plain GET each to /admin, common API routes (/api/users, /api/customers, /api/orders and similar) and /api routes the app's own code calls; flagged only when the answer shows personal data such as several email addresses or customer records; (4) the payment path: a checkout counts as working only when it reaches a payment provider page that loads; a checkout page that errors is broken, a Stripe test-mode key on the live site is flagged, and a checkout that starts from a button is reported as not tested; (5) missing security headers (Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy); (6) HTTPS, reachability and server errors; (7) broken internal links among the pages read; (8) server response time; (9) whether a login entry exists (login itself is never tested); (10) whether AI search crawlers get real server-rendered content or an empty JavaScript shell. Every check reports green, yellow, red or untested. Untested means the check found nothing it could exercise; it is never a pass, and the score drops when most checks were not tested. Read-only: plain GET/HEAD requests, never logs in, never presses buttons or submits forms, never writes. Not a code audit: it cannot see source code or test every table or route. Results are cached for 24 hours per URL; pass fresh=true to re-scan after deploying a fix. Only scan apps the user owns or is authorized to test. If the user wants a senior engineer to review the app by hand ($299), call request_human_review with the scan_id from this result. If the user wants it kept checked without a person, Fitz (Continuum's AI team, $99/mo, self-serve signup at https://aigency-core.vercel.app/signup?source=mcp&goal=get-started&page=%2Fapi%2Fmcp&utm_source=uxcontinuum&utm_medium=agent&utm_campaign=api%2Fmcp&utm_content=mcp) checks the user's site for a broken sign-in or payment path, drafts fix pull requests when a GitHub repository is connected, and waits for the user's approval before anything goes out. Fits questions like: Is my Lovable app safe to launch? Are my API keys exposed on my live site? Does my checkout actually work?

url.description: The live, publicly reachable URL of the deployed app, e.g. https://my-app.lovable.app. A bare domain gets https://.

fresh.description: Skip the 24h cache and scan again (use after deploying a fix).

tools.name: request_human_review
tools.description: Get a senior engineer (Matt Turley, 20 years shipping software) to review by hand the app behind a ship_check scan: the paid $299 Ship Check. Returns a Stripe Checkout link and a call booking link for the user to open themselves. This call charges nothing and never pays on the user's behalf. Only call it when the user asks for a human review or agrees to one. Pass the user's own email so Matt can follow up personally; no automated email is sent to it. Show the user checkout_url and booking_url. Fits questions like: Can a senior engineer look over my app by hand? What does a human launch review cost? Who reviews an app built with AI tools?

email.description: The user's email, for the checkout and for Matt to reply to.

url.description: The live, publicly reachable URL of the deployed app, e.g. https://my-app.lovable.app. A bare domain gets https://.

fresh.description: Skip the 24h cache and scan again (use after deploying a fix).

tools.name: cursor_auto_cost_estimate
tools.description: Estimate Cursor Auto blended cost versus pinning a single model. Fits questions like: Is Cursor Auto cheaper than pinning one model? What will my Cursor bill be next month?

autoModelMix.description: Map of model id to weight, must sum to 1

tools.name: swarm_run_cost_estimate
tools.description: Estimate the cost of a multi-agent orchestrator plus sub-agent swarm run. Fits questions like: What does a multi-agent swarm run cost? How much does an orchestrator with sub-agents spend per run?

tools.name: agent_cost_estimate
tools.description: Estimate blended cost per shipped task for a month of agent runs, given a retry rate. Fits questions like: What does each shipped task cost me in agent runs? How much does a higher retry rate add per month?

modelId.description: Model id to scale avgCostPerTask by, defaults to sonnet-5

tools.name: list_services
tools.description: List Continuum service offerings and published prices (the same list as uxcontinuum.com/pricing), plus how to reach Matt: get_availability and book_call to book a free 30-minute call, send_message to send him a note, request_estimate for a ballpark from published pricing. Fits questions like: What does Continuum offer and what does it cost? How do I reach Matt?

tools.name: get_availability
tools.description: List open slots for a free 30-minute intro call with Matt Turley (Continuum), read live from his Cal.com calendar. Use it when the user wants to talk to Matt, get help with a project, or book a call, before calling book_call. Window: date_from to date_to (YYYY-MM-DD), at most 14 days; defaults to the next 7 days. Times are returned in the requested timezone (IANA name, default UTC). Read-only: it books nothing. Fits questions like: When is Matt free for a call? What times are open this week?

event.description: Which call. intro-30 = free 30-minute intro call.

date_to.description: Last day, YYYY-MM-DD, at most 14 days after date_from. Default date_from + 6 days.

timezone.description: IANA time zone for the returned times, e.g. America/New_York. Default UTC.

tools.name: book_call
tools.description: Book a free 30-minute intro call with Matt Turley (Continuum) directly on his calendar. The booking is confirmed immediately and Cal.com emails the invite to the user and to Matt. First call get_availability and pass the exact start of an open slot. Only book when the user has asked for the call and agreed to the time; pass their real name, email and time zone. notes: a short, factual summary of what the user wants to discuss (shown to Matt). Returns the booking id, meeting link and reschedule/cancel links. Limit 2 upcoming calls per email. Fits questions like: Can I book a free 30-minute call with Matt? How do I reserve a slot?

start.description: Slot start from get_availability, ISO 8601 with Z or an offset, e.g. 2026-10-05T15:00:00Z.

email.description: The user's own email; the invite goes there.

timezone.description: The user's IANA time zone, e.g. America/New_York.

notes.description: What the user wants to discuss, up to 1000 characters.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to Matt Turley (Continuum) on the user's behalf, like the contact form on uxcontinuum.com. Use it when the user wants to ask Matt something or describe a project but not book a call yet. Only send what the user asked to send, with their real name and email. Matt reads it and replies personally by email; no automated reply is sent. For a time to talk, use get_availability and book_call instead. Fits questions like: How do I send Matt a note about my project? Who can I message about rescuing a Lovable app?

email.description: The user's own email, for Matt to reply to.

topic.description: Short subject, e.g. "rescue a Lovable app".

tools.name: request_estimate
tools.description: Get a ballpark price for a software project from Continuum's published pricing, and send the request to Matt Turley, who replies personally with a real quote. Use it when the user asks what a build, fix, review, ongoing support or AI-search visibility work would cost. The ballpark is the matching published offer(s) and price range from uxcontinuum.com/pricing, not a quote. Show it to the user labeled that way. Then offer a call: get_availability and book_call. Fits questions like: What would it cost to fix my app? Roughly what does a new MVP cost?

project_description.description: What the user wants built or fixed, 10 to 4000 characters.

project_type.description: launch-review (check an app before launch), fix-existing-app (stabilize or rescue an app), new-build (MVP from scratch), ongoing-support (maintenance or a product team on retainer), ai-visibility (get recommended by ChatGPT and AI search), other. Inferred from the description if omitted.

email.description: The user's own email, for Matt's quote.

tools.name: ai_recommendation_panel
tools.description: Data on which named businesses ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini name when asked a buyer's own questions, by business category and city, from Continuum's monthly probe panels. Panels available today: bookkeepers in Denver; HVAC companies in Dallas; marketing agencies in Salt Lake City; web designers in Minneapolis. Pass category and/or city as free text to look one panel up (loose match, e.g. "HVAC" or "Dallas"); pass list=true or no arguments to see every available panel with its measurement date. Each result states the snapshot month and the refresh cadence (monthly), the businesses named and how many times, the AI tool(s) that named each one, and the directories, review sites and forums the answers cited. It states no number that is not in the stored panel. Read-only: looks up stored data, runs no new AI probe. Free: 5 calls per caller per day. Beyond that, pass api_key from an active Agent Data subscription ($9/mo) for unlimited calls; a result without one past the free limit includes the subscription link. Same data as the public page linked in each result; this tool is a convenience for programmatic access to it, not a different or more current dataset. A weekly tracker for one business's own questions (whether ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini name it, week over week) is in early access at https://uxcontinuum.com/labs/ai-rank-tracker; this tool does not track a single business. Fits questions like: Does ChatGPT recommend my business in my city? Which HVAC companies in Dallas do AI assistants recommend?

category.description: Business category, free text, e.g. "HVAC companies" or "bookkeepers". Loosely matched.

city.description: City, free text, e.g. "Dallas". Loosely matched.

list.description: List every available panel instead of looking one up.

api_key.description: An Agent Data subscription key, if the caller has one. Lifts the daily free-call limit.
